entry.title: Democrat Haley Stevens endorses GOP's Mike Rogers in Michigan Senate race 2 days before election
entry.summary: Michigan Democrat Abdul El-Sayeds former opponent in the U.S. Senate primary, Haley Stevens, stunned party officials Sunday by endorsing Republican Mike Rogers after Democratic tensions boiled over days before the election that could determine the balance of power on Capitol Hill. WATCH | Stunning endorsement shakes up Michigan Senate race Stunning endorsement shakes up Michigan Senate race Stevens endorsed Rogers after attending a Detroit church service with him. The remarkable show of support for President Donald Trump's backed candidate in the tightly contested race comes after she was uninvited to a joint event the same day with El-Sayed, who defeated the congresswoman by a slim margin in the August primary. Our Democratic nominee for Senate said I was no longer welcome in his campaign and that I should stay away,' Stevens said video announcing the endorsement. And he's right. And that's why I am endorsing Mike Rogers for the United States Senate today. RELATED STORY | Democrats fear slippage with Black voters makes Michigan Senate race feel far closer than it should While Stevens has been critical of El-Sayeds comments surrounding Israel, she had recently reaffirmed she would vote for the former public health official who would be the countrys first Muslim senator if elected Tuesday. The fallout from her visit to Perfecting Church was swift, with her longtime chief of staff resigning and a number of staff members expected to follow soon, according to a person familiar with the developments who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss internal matters. As Stevens swayed alongside Rogers in the pews, El-Sayed was a few miles away at another church trying to present a united front with fellow Democrats. The Associated Press attended both services as the dramatic split-screen unfolded. The latest and late-stage infighting comes as Democrats look to drive turnout among Black and Jewish voters in key strongholds. El-Sayed, a former Michigan public health official, is in a tight race with Rogers, an ex-congressman, for the seat held by Democrat Gary Peters, who is retiring. Keeping Michigan in Democratic hands is vital to the partys effort to win a majority for the final two years of Trumps second term. United we stand, divided we fall, Rep. Debbie Dingell, D-Mich., had said hours earlier. Dueling church services: Stevens defects as Democrats preach unity Stevens was initially set to join the nominee and U.S. Rep. Jim Clyburn of South Carolina at a church
entry.article_text: Michigan Democrat Abdul El-Sayed’s former opponent in the U.S. Senate primary, Haley Stevens, stunned party officials Sunday by endorsing Republican Mike Rogers after Democratic tensions boiled over days before the election that could determine the balance of power on Capitol Hill.WATCH | Stunning endorsement shakes up Michigan Senate raceStevens endorsed Rogers after attending a Detroit church service with him. The remarkable show of support for President Donald Trump's backed candidate in the tightly contested race comes after she was uninvited to a joint event the same day with El-Sayed, who defeated the congresswoman by a slim margin in the August primary.“Our Democratic nominee for Senate said I was no longer welcome in his campaign and that I should stay away," Stevens said video announcing the endorsement. And that's why I am endorsing Mike Rogers for the United States Senate today.”RELATED STORY | Democrats fear slippage with Black voters makes Michigan Senate race feel ‘far closer than it should’While Stevens has been critical of El-Sayed’s comments surrounding Israel, she had recently reaffirmed she would vote for the former public health official who would be the country’s first Muslim senator if elected Tuesday. The fallout from her visit to Perfecting Church was swift, with her longtime chief of staff resigning and a number of staff members expected to follow soon, according to a person familiar with the developments who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss internal matters.As Stevens swayed alongside Rogers in the pews, El-Sayed was a few miles away at another church trying to present a united front with fellow Democrats. The Associated Press attended both services as the dramatic split-screen unfolded.The latest and late-stage infighting comes as Democrats look to drive turnout among Black and Jewish voters in key strongholds. El-Sayed, a former Michigan public health official, is in a tight race with Rogers, an ex-congressman, for the seat held by Democrat Gary Peters, who is retiring. Keeping Michigan in Democratic hands is vital to the party’s effort to win a majority for the final two years of Trump’s second term.“United we stand, divided we fall,” Rep. Debbie Dingell, D-Mich., had said hours earlier.Dueling church services: Stevens defects as Democrats preach unityStevens was initially set to join the nominee and U.S. Jim Clyburn of South Carolina at a church event. Turkish said last week that he was going to vote for Rogers, arguing that El-Sayed had not done enough to address the Jewish community's concerns.The appearance stunned Democrats across the political spectrum, coming just days after Stevens publicly reaffirmed that she would vote for El-Sayed.Meanwhile, El-Sayed attended a separate church service alongside Dingell, South Carolina Rep. Jim Clyburn, Maryland Sen. Angela Alsobrooks and state Sen. Mallory McMorrow, who dropped out of the Democratic Senate primary before voting began.El-Sayed spoke for nearly 10 minutes at the service, but did not address the latest controversy.“It’s in churches like this, in pews like the ones in which you sit, that the foundation of my life was built,” El-Sayed said.Dingell, a senior Democratic figure in the state who helped organize the planned joint appearance in hopes of bringing together Democrats in the final days before Tuesday's vote, said she asked Stevens not to attend and that Stevens told her she would abide by that.“I'm the one who pulled it because it had become way too distracting," Dingell said a telephone interview Sunday before Stevens' appearance. “This is not how I was going to spend my weekend before the election, to be perfectly frank.”"The bishop was getting upset, because this is a real church service,” Dingell added.The latest and late-stage infighting comes as Democrats look to drive turnout among Black and Jewish voters in key strongholds. El-Sayed, a former Michigan public health official, is in a tight race with Republican Mike Rogers, an ex-congressman, for the seat held by Democrat Gary Peters, who is retiring. Keeping Michigan in Democratic hands is vital to the party's effort to win a majority for the final two years of Trump's second term.Dingell and other Democrats insist the party is united behind El-Sayed. Early voting has been underway since Oct. 24, before the latest tensions erupted. But the renewed bickering has complicated Democrats’ efforts to deliver a unified closing message in crucial areas such as Detroit, where turnout could prove decisive.“Whenever anyone tries to set us against each other, we have an obligation to stand up and fight back,” Stevens wrote in a statement late Friday that ended with: “Go vote!”The tensions carry particular significance in Wayne County, which includes Detroit, and neighboring Oakland County. Stevens defeated El-Sayed in both counties in the August primary, drawing support from Black and Jewish voters who are important parts of the Democratic coalition.How did we get here?The Democratic primary was among the most bitter this year. Each candidate accused the other of making personal attacks. Tens of millions of dollars in outside spending poured into the race, including from the American Israel Public Affairs Committee’s affiliated super PAC, which backed Stevens. El-Sayed took particular offense to an outside group’s ad accusing him of disrespecting women.Although Stevens pledged after the primary to help El-Sayed however she could, the two have not appeared together publicly since a unity breakfast two days after his summer win.Their lack of joint appearances was particularly notable as some Jewish voters and leaders continued to criticize El-Sayed over his comments about Israel, past rhetoric and campaign appearances with controversial streamer Hasan Piker.The divisions spilled into public view again Wednesday when Stevens’ fiancé told The Detroit News that he would vote for Rogers. Hours later, Stevens appeared on CNN to reaffirm her support for El-Sayed but urged his campaign to “shut out the hate and call it out.”Dingell had been working to bring them together at church alongside Clyburn, one of the nation’s most prominent Black Democrats.But on Friday, after The Associated Press reported on the planned joint appearance, Stevens released a lengthy statement calling on El-Sayed to condemn an ad by an independent left-wing group that linked U.S. support for Israel to high grocery prices.“Abdul promises to get money out of politics,” Stevens wrote. “He can begin by getting Israel out of his explanation for everything Michigan cannot afford.”El-Sayed then responded: “So while Congresswoman Stevens seems intent on relitigating a primary that ended three months ago, let’s all focus on the task at hand.”He repeated Saturday evening that the ad was not made by his campaign and “I do not agree with the contents of that ad.”Michigan Democrats insist they are unitedDespite the latest tensions, El-Sayed planned to move ahead with a series of church visits Sunday alongside Clyburn and other prominent Black Democrats.The appearances will also include Detroit Mayor Mary Sheffield, Garlin Gilchrist II, the nominee for secretary of state, and several Michigan bishops, according to campaign advisories obtained by AP.Democrats are seeking to drive turnout in Detroit, where roughly three-quarters of residents are Black and strong support is essential to Democratic success statewide.

entry.title: Deputies locate wanted Broward County man after Fort Pierce hotel disturbance - cw34.com
entry.summary: Deputies locate wanted Broward County man after Fort Pierce hotel disturbance    cw34.com
entry.article_text: A report of a woman being assaulted and pushed into a car at a Fort Pierce hotel led deputies to a Broward County man wanted in four felony probation cases, authorities said. Deputies say they were called to the Best Western in the 7900 block of South U.S. Highway 1 around 11:20 p.m. Friday after a witness reported seeing a man assault a woman, push her into a vehicle, and drive away, according to the St. Lucie County Sheriff’s Office . Deputies reportedly confirmed a battery had occurred and identified the suspect as 37-year-old Guyrson Maddy of Broward County. A records check found an active warrant for probation violations in four separate felony cases dating from 2017 to 2025. See also: Rescue crews search Delray Beach pond after car found submerged Court records show Maddy’s criminal history dates back to 2012. It includes cases involving battery on a law enforcement officer, grand theft of a motor vehicle, third-degree grand theft, and organized fraud. Investigators also identified a dark-colored 2025 Tesla Model Y they believed was involved. Deputies found a vehicle matching that description at a home on Palm Breezes Drive. A woman at the home confirmed she had been at the hotel and directed deputies to a bathroom where they found Maddy. Deputy Mendoza and his K-9 partner, Oso, helped find him. Maddy followed deputies’ commands and was arrested without incident, the sheriff’s office said. Maddy is being held at the St. Lucie County Jail on a domestic battery charge, with Broward County holds for probation violations.

entry.title: NTSB to hold news conference at 1 p.m. regarding Learjet 60 crash in Palm Beach County
entry.summary: The National Transportation Safety Board will hold a news conference Monday afternoon to discuss its investigation into Sunday's deadly Learjet crash in Palm Beach County. NTSB Member Tom Chapman is scheduled to brief members of the media at 1 p.m. at the Palm Beach County Emergency Operations Center at 20 S. Military Trail in West Palm Beach. LATEST REPORT BELOW: 9 killed after jet crashes and erupts into flames in Palm Beach County, Florida The briefing comes a day after a Learjet 60 crashed Sunday near Greenacres and Palm Springs, killing nine people aboard. According to the NTSB, Chapman is expected to discuss the investigative process and outline the work investigators plan to conduct at the crash site in the coming days. The agency has not provided additional information in this announcement about what may have caused the crash. WATCH BELOW: Gov. DeSantis speaks about tragedy Gov. Ron DeSantis speaks after deadly Learjet crash in Palm Beach County The NTSB investigates aviation accidents and determines their probable causes. Monday's briefing is expected to focus on the early stages of the investigation rather than a final determination of what led to the crash. The aircraft had departed Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was headed to North Eleuthera Airport in the Bahamas. Video showed the plane crashing on a road at a high rate of speed at 12:50 p.m., producing a massive fireball. Hundreds of residents were expected to be displaced by the crash , and a major stretch of Military Trail remains closed. No fatalities were reported on the ground. Stay with WPTV.com and WPTV News for more details as they become available.

entry.title: In Kansas, a data center backlash is uniting voters across the political aisle
entry.summary: Like most Kansans, Carrie Schmidt enthusiastically supported President Donald Trump in past elections. I voted for him, she told Scripps News in an interview Wednesday. I was very, like, loud. But her views on the president have soured in recent months and she says theres one main issue that explains why. I don't trust President Trump to make the best decisions right now, especially when he's saying that he supports these data centers, Schmidt said. Schmidt is one of a growing number of Americans opposed to the proliferation of data center developments, used to power the internet and, increasingly, artificial intelligence technologies. Though the construction projects bring the promise of new jobs and added tax revenue for communities, many residents are growing firmer in their opposition, citing concerns about increased utility costs, health impacts and a broader cultural clash with rural values. Schmidt didnt initially intend to become an anti-data center activist, she says. In April, she saw a Facebook post about a data center project planned in her town of Gardner, and began to research more about the developments. That project was ultimately scrapped amid opposition from local residents. But it put Schmidt a chiropractic assistant with no prior experience in political organizing on a path towards activism, one which landed her on the receiving end of a lawsuit. Shortly after the Gardner project was killed, Schmidt learned of a separate data center development planned in nearby Edgerton, a small town of fewer than 2,000 people, roughly 45 minutes southwest of Kansas City. She and Edgerton resident Kim Twente got connected on an anti-data center Facebook page and joined forces to organize against the project, gathering signatures for a petition to force city leaders to either scrap the development or put it up for a public vote. But city officials instead pursued a third option: suing Schmidt and Twente, asking a judge to declare their petition void and invalid, arguing it went beyond their legal authorities. DAMAC Digital, the UAE-based company seeking to develop the project, soon intervened, working with the city to block the petition from reaching voters. Because state law is not clear on whether this specific proposal counts as administrative, the City is proactively asking a District Court judge to step in and decide if the proposed ordinance is valid, Edgerton leaders wrote in an unsigned July statement. entry.title: 9 dead after Learjet crashes near Greenacres; shelters open for hundreds displaced
entry.summary: A Learjet carrying nine people crashed in a residential area near Cresthaven on Sunday afternoon, according to the Federal Aviation Administration. WATCH WPTV'S BREAKING NEWS COVERAGE BELOW: Learjet headed to Bahamas crashes in Palm Beach County with 9 people on board The FAA said the Learjet 60 crashed around 12:50 p.m. The aircraft had departed Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was headed to North Eleuthera Airport in the Bahamas. Nine people were on board, according to the FAA. The agency said its information is preliminary and subject to change. Gov. Ron DeSantis visited the scene Sunday and described the crash as 'cataclysmic,' saying the aircraft appeared 'like a missile going down' and left a large crater along Military Trail. He praised Palm Beach County first responders for their quick response. Officials said they had not received reports at the time of the news conference of people on the ground being killed or injured by the crash or debris. DeSantis said the debris field stretched a significant distance. Palm Beach County officials said approximately 600 people in a nearby mobile home community are expected to be relocated because the crash site is considered a crime scene while authorities investigate. Officials said two shelters were on standby and Palm Tran was prepared to transport residents once law enforcement allowed the evacuation to begin. Military Trail closed until further notice Palm Beach County said Military Trail between 10th Avenue North and Purdy Lane/Alameda Drive will remain closed until further notice. Only emergency vehicles will be allowed into the closed area. Law enforcement will redirect traffic and assist residents as needed. Drivers are being asked to use 10th Avenue North and Purdy Lane/Alameda Drive for east-west travel and Haverhill Road and Kirk Road for north-south travel. County officials said they are also working on an alternate traffic pattern expected to be released as the response continues. During Sunday's news conference, a county commissioner said the crash created a massive crater on Military Trail and cautioned that portions of the roadway could face an extended closure. County officials stressed that the timeline will also depend on the federal investigation. The FAA and National Transportation Safety Board will investigate the crash. The NTSB will lead the investigation and provide further updates.

entry.title: Martin County woman honored after using CPR to save 3-year-old girl from swimming pool - WPTV
entry.summary: Martin County woman honored after using CPR to save 3-year-old girl from swimming pool    WPTV
entry.article_text: A 20-year-old Martin County woman is being honored after she used CPR to help save a 3-year-old girl she found motionless at the bottom of a swimming pool. Nearly two months after the August rescue, Martin County Fire Rescue recognized Madison Isler with the department's Heroic Heart Award.WATCH: Martin County woman honored for saving 3-year-oldThe rescue happened Aug. 23 as Isler walked past the pool at her apartment complex. She told WPTV something in the water caught her attention."It kind of looked like a smudge in your sunglasses," Isler said. "And then, so I took my glasses off, and I looked, and then I realized that it was a little girl."That little girl was 3-year-old Luna.Isler said Luna was motionless at the bottom of the swimming pool when she spotted her."I jumped in and grabbed her and pulled her out, and she was blue," Isler said.Isler called for her boyfriend to contact 911 and began CPR, using skills she said she learned at a young age from her parents, who both work in fire rescue."You just don't really think; you just kind of do, especially in a situation when it's a little baby," Isler said. "I pulled a lifeless baby out of a pool."A family friend who is a pediatric intensive care unit nurse heard the commotion and joined the rescue effort, according to the account shared by Martin County Fire Rescue."Together, they continued their life-saving efforts till finally Luna responded," Martin County Fire Rescue Chief Chad Cianciulli said.Fire rescue officials said Luna was alert and oriented by the time paramedics transported her to the hospital.Luna's mother, Christine Hernandez, said she is grateful Isler happened to be nearby when her daughter needed help."It's God's work that He put her when we needed her, like at the right place at the right time," Hernandez said.Nearly two months after that frightening day, Isler and Luna reunited at Martin County Fire Rescue headquarters.This time, they were together to celebrate the outcome of the rescue.Martin County Fire Rescue presented Isler with its Heroic Heart Award to recognize her actions."Today, on behalf of Martin County Fire Rescue and our entire community, we honor Madison for her courage to act with Martin County Fire Rescue's Heroic Heart Award," Cianciulli said during the recognition.According to the department, Isler is the first person to receive its Heroic Heart Award.For Isler, however, the recognition is secondary to seeing Luna alive and able to grow up."What means the most to me is that Luna's here with us today and that she gets to grow up and experience life," Isler said.Isler affectionately calls Luna her "unicorn baby."For Hernandez, the outcome comes with overwhelming gratitude."I'm just very, very thankful, very thankful for Maddie and her family," Hernandez said.For Isler, a skill learned years before an emergency ever happened became critical in the moment Luna needed help, turning CPR training into an action Martin County Fire Rescue says helped save a child's life.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. Our editorial team verifies all reporting on all platforms for fairness and accuracy.

entry.summary: More than 15 inches of rain was reported in parts of Palm Beach Gardens, Riviera Beach and The Acreage over approximately 12 hours, leaving roads flooded and prompting officials to urge residents to stay off the streets. The City of Palm Beach Gardens said some roadways were impassable Monday because of standing water, while other areas could only be accessed by emergency vehicles or heavy equipment. LATEST FORECAST BELOW: WPTV First Alert Weather Forecast for Afternoon of Monday, Nov. 2, 2026 City officials said the reported rainfall was exceptionally rare. According to the city, NOAA Atlas 14 data indicates 13 inches of rain represents a 1-in-100-year event, while the reported 15 inches exceeds that threshold and approaches a 1-in-200-year event. Police, Fire Rescue, Public Works and Engineering personnel have been monitoring conditions since Sunday afternoon, according to the city. Despite flooding on area roads, officials said the city's stormwater system was performing as designed and helping reduce the risk of flooding to homes and properties. As of 10:40 a.m. Monday, water levels were subsiding in Steeplechase, but isolated areas still had approximately 12 to 15 inches of water. Some roads there were accessible only to emergency medical vehicles. Horseshoe Acres also had isolated areas with approximately 12 to 15 inches of water, with some locations accessible only by emergency vehicles. The city reported several other problem areas: Cypress Hollow: Significant flooding, with access limited to Public Works heavy equipment. PGA Boulevard west of Mirasol: Flooding in both eastbound and westbound directions. The Florida Department of Transportation was notified. PGA National: Some areas had approximately 12 to 15 inches of water and were passable by emergency vehicles. Impacted areas included Avenue of Champions, Avenue of Masters, Tournament Avenue and Lexington Green. Montecito: Approximately 8 inches of standing water, although the city said motorists could proceed with caution. entry.title: Midterm elections pit Iowans’ economic struggles against conservative values
entry.summary: As the white Jeep SUV pulled into Richmond Ave., a quiet street on the northeast end of town, our target soon became clear: there, behind the well-manicured grass yard, sat a small, shingled house, each window filled edge-to-edge with union signage: This Union Home Supports Rob Sand and Steelworkers for Turek, among them. Waiting for us out front was Wilson, a member of the United Steelworkers Local 310, soon to be greeted by Josh Turek, a state senator vying for the U.S. Senate. A former paralympian who, born with spina bifida, uses a wheelchair, Turek quickly made his way over to chat. It was the kind of choreographed encounter the Turek campaign was expecting; Scripps News on Saturday was granted exclusive access to trail Turek and AFL-CIO President Liz Shuler as they knocked on voters doors, following the launch of a union get-out-the-vote effort earlier that morning. But as Wilson shared with Turek his efforts to gin up support for Democrats up and down the ballot, the two flanked by several campaign staff and videographers hoping to catch a viral moment, my eyes soon turned to the house immediately west of Wilsons. Its yard was in considerably worse condition, the front porch littered with old toys and empty energy drink bottles. Standing out front were two women and a young baby, watching the events next door with both curiosity and distance. IN CASE YOU MISSED IT | Trump reverses course, will hold rallies in Kansas and Iowa after all One woman, the elder of the two, introduced herself as Traci Cone. She worked at a nearby medical device manufacturer and was struggling to make ends meet, she said. If you have rent and a car payment plus all your other bills, $14 an hour ain't even close to what you need to pay all that, Cone told Scripps News. After you pay all your other bills so that you have a roof over your head, you don't have a lot left for groceries. And when you go to the store and spend 50 bucks and come out with two bags, that's not enough, Cone continued. Her eyes began to fill with tears, her voice choking up: Yeah, it's a struggle Economic troubles present political opportunities Cone is not alone in her struggle. Inflation in the midwest region, which includes Iowa, has climbed higher than almost anywhere else in the country since the Iran war began, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. Iowans wages, meanwhile, have not kept pace, lagging especially in Polk County, which includes Des Moines. Those realities present an opportuni
entry.article_text: Iowans’ wages, meanwhile, have not kept pace, lagging especially in Polk County, which includes Des Moines.Those realities present an opportunity for Democrats in Iowa — a state that has seen a steady rightward shift over the past decade and that Trump handily carried in the past three presidential elections.“The economic issues that Trump was talking about last time around really did appeal to working people because they were struggling with the same things we're struggling with today,” Shuler told Scripps News from the car between pre-selected door-knocking sites. “This time, it's completely different, because the issues, the kitchen table bread and butter issues that people are struggling with, are the campaign.”The Democratic candidates running for office seem to agree: Turek, gubernatorial nominee Rob Sand, Congressional candidates Sarah Trone Garriott, Lindsay James and Christina Bohannan all have made prices and affordability the centerpiece of their campaigns.RELATED STORY | Democrats tout momentum as early voting rises ahead of midterms“Everywhere I'm going, I'm hearing the same things: this state is uniquely hurting,” Turek said at the union worker rally.

entry.title: Aerial video shows significant flooding in St. Lucie West; police urge drivers to avoid area
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie police are urging drivers to avoid portions of St. Lucie West as significant water accumulation creates hazardous conditions on area roadways. The Port St. Lucie Police Department said in a post on its Facebook page that several roads have become difficult to navigate because of high water and asked motorists to stay out of the area unless travel is absolutely necessary. Police said officers are responding to reports of vehicles stranded in high-water conditions. Drivers are being warned not to attempt to travel through standing water. Police are advising motorists who encounter flooding to turn around and find an alternate route. 'Never underestimate the depth or power of floodwaters,' the department said in its news release. Police said officers are continuing to monitor conditions and will provide updates as road closures and other traffic impacts develop. Residents are also being asked to stay off the roads if possible and give emergency responders room to work. The flooding comes amid heavy rain affecting the Treasure Coast, with areas receiving repeated rounds of downpours.

entry.article_text: Lucie Public Schools will dismiss students one hour early Monday and cancel all after-school activities as heavy rainfall and flooding continue to impact the county. The district announced that all students will be dismissed one hour earlier than their regularly scheduled dismissal times. All after-school activities, including aftercare programs, have also been canceled. The changes come after parts of St. Lucie County received up to 6 inches of rain. Earlier Monday, the district announced that parents and guardians could pick up their children early, with one exception. Oak Hammock K-8 School is not allowing early pickups because of flooding in front of the school, according to the district. It was not immediately clear how the flooding would affect the school's updated dismissal schedule. See also: Boca Raton co-pilot, 20, killed in fiery Florida jet crash, family confirms The district says all student absences Monday will be excused. Families are urged to plan for adjusted dismissal times and monitor the district's website and social media channels for updates.

entry.title: Brightline temporarily suspends service between Orlando and West Palm Beach due to high water
entry.summary: Brightline temporarily suspended train service between Orlando and West Palm Beach because of high water along its rail corridor in Brevard County. The rail company said maintenance crews are at the scene and service will resume when conditions allow trains to safely travel through the affected area. LATEST FORECAST BELOW: WPTV First Alert Weather Forecast for Afternoon of Monday, Nov. 2, 2026 Brightline said its rail infrastructure teams are monitoring conditions along the corridor in coordination with Florida East Coast Railway. Once water levels recede, crews will inspect tracks, signals and crossings in the affected area before passenger trains are allowed to resume service. Brightline did not provide an estimated time for service between Orlando and West Palm Beach to resume. Service between Miami, Aventura, Fort Lauderdale, Boca Raton and West Palm Beach is operating normally, according to the company. Passengers with reservations affected by the suspension will be contacted directly about their travel options. Brightline is encouraging passengers to check its website, mobile app and social media channels for the latest service information. The disruption comes as heavy rain affects parts of Florida's east coast, bringing flooding concerns to portions of the state.

entry.title: Heavy rain floods Port St. Lucie, Okeechobee roads amid Treasure Coast flood watch - WPEC
entry.summary: Heavy rain floods Port St. Lucie, Okeechobee roads amid Treasure Coast flood watch    WPEC
entry.article_text: Floodwaters are creating dangerous driving conditions across Port St. Lucie and Okeechobee County, leaving vehicles stranded, roads underwater, and officials urging residents to stay home as more heavy rain threatens the region Monday. Lucie , police said officers are responding to a significant number of calls involving vehicles stranded in floodwaters as widespread flooding impacts neighborhoods and major roadways. Lucie Police Department is urging residents to avoid unnecessary travel while emergency personnel respond to flooding throughout the city. According to police, the following areas are experiencing flooding: Southwest Airoso Boulevard Southeast Thornhill Drive and surrounding side streets Southworth Boulevard and Jeanette Drive Country Club Estates Southwest Discovery Way and Community Boulevard in Tradition LTC Parkway Police warned that floodwaters have created hazardous driving conditions and urged motorists not to underestimate the depth or movement of water covering roads. "Turn around, don't drown!" the department reminded residents. See also: Boca Raton co-pilot, 20, killed in fiery Florida jet crash, family confirms Officials said drivers whose vehicles become stranded in floodwaters can contact a towing company directly if they are not in immediate danger and do not require an emergency rescue. Residents with questions about school closures are being advised to contact their schools directly. Lucie intersection closed The flooding has also prompted the closure of the intersection of Southwest California Boulevard and Southwest Savona Boulevard. Water has also been reported on Traditional Parkway, Community Boulevard, Volucia Drive, and Innovation Way. The roads are still open, but crews and police are assessing the conditions. City officials said crews are checking drainage systems to ensure water is flowing properly and addressing potholes found or reported throughout the area. Motorists are being urged to avoid the intersection and use alternate routes. See also: GALLERY: Flooded roads creating challenges for drivers in Palm Beach County The city also warned drivers not to remove barricades or attempt to travel through closed roadways. Residents who encounter potholes are being advised to avoid the affected area and call 911, according to the city's announcement. Flood watch remains in effect across the Treasure Coast According to the National Weather Service in Melbourne, east-central Florida, including Indian River County, remains under a flood watch until 7 p.m. Forecasters expect an additional 1 to 3 inches of rainfall, with some locations facing a 10% chance of receiving 5 inches or more. In Indian River County, officials are warning residents to prepare for scattered to widespread showers and thunderstorms, with periods of heavy rainfall that could lead to localized flooding of roads and low-lying areas. According to county officials, the primary weather hazards include: Heavy rainfall and localized flooding. Wind gusts of 25 to 40 mph. Dangerous beach and marine conditions. Officials said the potential for heavy rainfall and flooding could continue through Tuesday. Residents are being urged to secure loose outdoor items, allow extra travel time, slow down on wet roads and keep multiple ways to receive weather alerts. With the ground already saturated from previous rainfall, additional storms could quickly lead to standing water on roadways and worsening flooding conditions. Lucie officials are encouraging residents to monitor the city's website and the Port St. Lucie Police Department's social media channels for updates on traffic conditions and potential road closures. Okeechobee County roads remain underwater Meanwhile, several major roadways in Okeechobee County remain underwater, with officials warning that flooding could continue for several days, even after the weather improves. Authorities said warning signs have been placed in affected areas, but motorists should use extreme caution. According to county officials, the following major roads are experiencing flooding: State Road 68 East: The roadway is underwater from the 3000 block to the 15000 block. State Road 70 East: Water is covering the roadway in the 11000 block near Posey's Corner. Highway 441 North: The roadway is underwater near Potter Road. Officials stressed that these are only some of the major roads affected by flooding. Numerous local and residential streets throughout Okeechobee County also remain flooded, with some completely submerged and potentially impassable. Motorists are being warned not to assume roads outside the listed areas are safe. Floodwaters are expected to continue rising in some areas, while others remain at critical levels. Floodwaters could damage roadways County officials also warned that many roads have been saturated or submerged for more than 24 hours, raising concerns about damage to pavement and underlying road structures. Prolonged exposure to floodwaters can weaken road surfaces, while standing water can conceal washouts, pavement deterioration and other hazards. Authorities said a road that was passable earlier may no longer be safe to travel. Drivers who must travel are being urged to significantly reduce their speed and avoid flooded roadways whenever possible. Officials warned that driving too fast through standing water increases the risk of hydroplaning and losing control of a vehicle. Vehicles traveling through flooded streets can also create waves that push additional water into nearby homes and properties, worsening flooding for residents. Officials urge residents to stay home Emergency officials are strongly discouraging unnecessary travel and asking residents not to drive around neighborhoods simply to survey storm damage or flooding. Residents are being urged to remain home whenever possible, avoid barricaded roads and allow emergency personnel to continue responding to storm-related hazards. A unified public safety update was expected following an 8 a.m. meeting to discuss storm impacts and current conditions. entry.title: Trump administration asks Supreme Court to intervene in California ballot case
entry.summary: President Donald Trump's administration appealed to the Supreme Court on Monday in its push to sideline thousands of disputed California mail ballots the day before the pivotal midterm elections. The emergency appeal came after an appeals court rejected the request to set aside some 20,000 ballots from people the federal government suspects may not be citizens. The federal government says those ballots should not be counted until the voters status can be verified. California officials say the list is highly unreliable and likely includes many people who are U.S. citizens. The Republican Trump administration has prioritized identifying noncitizen voters this year, despite them being rare. A district court judge forcefully denied the Justice Department's request and warned that the demand could disenfranchise citizens in the Nov. 3 midterm elections to determine control of Congress. The Justice Department asked the high court for a limited injunction that would direct California to stop commingling suspected illegal ballots with legal ones while the case continues to play out. Voting has been underway in California, a largely Democratic state, since early October. All of the states roughly 23 million registered voters are mailed a ballot. Hundreds of thousands of ballots have already been processed. IN CASE YOU MISSED IT | Immigrants seeking US citizenship caught up in California voter fraud crackdown Lower courts have sided with the state, with a district judge warning that segregating ballots would wreak havoc on the midterm elections and erode trust in the democratic process. If the Executive can discount votes and threaten an ongoing election due to unproven allegations, then our democracy is in danger, U.S. District Judge David O. Carter wrote. The Justice Department has sought to move the case along quickly, unsuccessfully asking an appeals court to intervene early. The Trump administration has racked up a series of wins in emergency appeals before the Supreme Court, but the justices previously rejected the presidents push to restrict mail ballots ahead of the midterms.

Regardless, she added, it’s too late for the courts to force such a major change on the eve of an election.The Trump administration in its suit argued the presence of a spoiler candidate with the same name as the GOP incumbent warranted a court-ordered investigation into the results if Sen. Sullivan lost.WATCH | Court battles loom ahead of Election DayGleason, a nominee of former President Barack Obama, wrote, “The United States provides no workable plan as to how it proposes to segregate ballots cast for Daniel J. Sullivan on Election Day and then conduct a court-ordered unspecified ‘investigation’ of those ballots in a manner that would preserve voter secrecy,”The ruling is the latest legal setback for the Trump administration in its efforts to inject itself in to states’ voting processes in the final days of the midterm elections. A federal appeals court on Friday rejected a Justice Department demand that California election officials set aside ballots from 20,000 people the administration claims could be noncitizens.RELATED STORY | Alaska governor orders investigation into ‘Dan Sullivan’ ballot controversyThe Justice Department on Sunday quickly filed a notice of appeal following the district court’s ruling.“Alaskan voters deserve a fair election, not to be misled in an attempt to rig outcomes,” a Justice Department spokesperson said.Trump said he had not heard about the ruling while speaking to reporters on the tarmac outside of Air Force One after he landed in Iowa for a campaign rally Sunday, but described the DOJ’s case as “one of the most meritful things,” and a “very important lawsuit.”Meanwhile, the courts have also imposed restrictions on the Trump administration’s efforts to hunt for alleged voter fraud and on the DOJ’s threats to local election officials that they could face criminal penalties over noncitizen voting. A federal judge late Friday imposed a sweeping emergency order restricting the Justice Department and the Department of Homeland Security from demanding that election officials in any state segregate ballots, purge voters from voter rolls, or halt ballot processing.US District Judge Trina Thompson, an appointee of President Joe Biden, also ruled that the Trump administration cannot “threaten, intimidate or coerce” election officials to demand changes in ballot processing procedures on claims voters are ineligible. The Justice Department has appealed the ruling.New allegations in Alaska Senate raceThe Alaska Senate race, in which Democrat Mary Peltola is trying to unseat Sullivan, was roiled this week by a New York Times report with new details about Democratic involvement in getting Daniel J. Sullivan onto the ballot in a race that could determine which party controls the Senate.While the civil case played out, the Justice Department also accelerated its criminal probe into the alleged Democratic efforts, and the state’s Republican governor ordered an investigation, while suggesting he could oppose certification depending on the results of the probe.IN CASE YOU MISSED IT | Report: Peltola campaign linked to effort to recruit second Dan Sullivan in Alaska Senate raceAlaska officials, Democratic groups and nonpartisan voter advocacy organizations that all opposed the DOJ lawsuit argued the administration had no legal right to drag a federal court into a dispute over Daniel J. Sullivan’s candidacy that had been settled with state court litigation several months ago.They argued the DOJ put forward no evidence that voters were confused by his inclusion — particularly as election administrators included several identifiers on the ballot to distinguish him from Sen. Sullivan.While the Justice Department argued in its lawsuit that the presence of two Sullivans could confuse voters, Gleason wrote in her decision Sunday that voters in fact would be confused if Alaska segregated Daniel J. Sullivan ballots as the Justice Department sought.“Clearly, if this Court were to order that certain ballots will be segregated and subject to a future and as yet unspecified investigation by law enforcement, it would likely result in voter, ‘confusion and consequent incentive to remain away from the polls,’” Gleason wrote. “Such late-breaking changes to the election rules are strongly disfavored.”The-CNN-Wire™ & © 2026 Cable News Network, Inc., a Warner Bros.

entry.title: NTSB: Learjet 60 crew reported icing, turbulence shortly before deadly Palm Beach County crash
entry.summary: The crew of a Learjet that crashed in Palm Beach County on Sunday reported icing, moderate turbulence and precipitation minutes before the aircraft rapidly descended and crashed, killing all nine people aboard, federal investigators said Monday. During a Monday afternoon news conference, National Transportation Safety Board Member Tom Chapman laid out a preliminary timeline of the Learjet 60's final flight and said weather conditions will be a major focus of the investigation. WATCH THE NTSB news conference below: NTSB holds news conference on Learjet crash in Palm Beach County Investigators also have some evidence that the aircraft began breaking apart before impact, although Chapman stressed the NTSB is still working to determine exactly what happened. The Learjet 60 was operated by Aurora Aviation doing business as Upper Jets, according to Chapman. The plane left Austin-Bergstrom International Airport at approximately 10:37 a.m. ET Sunday, bound for North Eleuthera in the Bahamas. There were nine people aboard, including two flight crew members and seven passengers. The NTSB said at approximately 12:47 p.m., the crew told air traffic controllers they were encountering light clear icing that they considered manageable, along with moderate turbulence. The aircraft was flying at 35,000 feet when the crew reported altitude deviations of approximately 700 feet. They also reported an outside temperature of minus 53 degrees Fahrenheit. Shortly afterward, the crew reported encountering precipitation and asked to climb to 37,000 feet. Air traffic control approved the request. 'Less than 30 seconds later, a transmission from the airplane announced the descent, followed by a mayday call,' Chapman said. WATCH BELOW: Gov. DeSantis speaks about tragedy Gov. Ron DeSantis speaks after deadly Learjet crash in Palm Beach County At about 12:48 p.m., investigators said the crew reported the aircraft was in an overspeed condition and descending. Later communications indicated it was rapidly losing altitude. The plane crashed at approximately 12:51 p.m. All nine people aboard were killed. Chapman said investigators are examining whether the icing and turbulence played a role in the crash. 'The weather conditions are a major focus of the investigation,' Chapman said, adding that investigators still need to determine what conditions were like at the plane's cruising altitude. There were nine people aboard, including two flight crew members and seven passengers.The NTSB said at approximately 12:47 p.m., the crew told air traffic controllers they were encountering light clear icing that they considered manageable, along with moderate turbulence.The aircraft was flying at 35,000 feet when the crew reported altitude deviations of approximately 700 feet. They also reported an outside temperature of minus 53 degrees Fahrenheit.Shortly afterward, the crew reported encountering precipitation and asked to climb to 37,000 feet. Air traffic control approved the request."Less than 30 seconds later, a transmission from the airplane announced the descent, followed by a mayday call," Chapman said.WATCH BELOW: Gov. DeSantis speaks about tragedyAt about 12:48 p.m., investigators said the crew reported the aircraft was in an overspeed condition and descending. Later communications indicated it was rapidly losing altitude.The plane crashed at approximately 12:51 p.m.All nine people aboard were killed.Chapman said investigators are examining whether the icing and turbulence played a role in the crash."The weather conditions are a major focus of the investigation," Chapman said, adding that investigators still need to determine what conditions were like at the plane's cruising altitude.The NTSB has not yet confirmed whether the aircraft flew through an active thunderstorm.Chapman said investigators have "some evidence that there was some breakup of the aircraft before impact," but cautioned that the investigation remains in its early stages.The debris field was described as roughly a half-mile by four-tenths of a mile, with debris found around ball fields, businesses and residences.Investigators have not yet identified all of the aircraft pieces recovered from the scene.NTSB Investigator-in-Charge Timothy Monville said one person on the ground suffered a leg injury. The person had been inside a vehicle leaving the area immediately adjacent to the crash site, according to information provided to investigators.Investigators are also trying to determine whether a cockpit voice recorder was aboard the aircraft when it crashed.Chapman said maintenance records indicate one had been installed, but investigators still need to confirm it remained aboard the plane.If recovered, Chapman said information from the recorder could become an important part of the investigation.About 20 NTSB investigators began arriving in Palm Beach County Sunday evening, with additional personnel arriving Monday.The investigative team includes specialists in aircraft systems and structures, recorders, weather and air traffic control, as well as a drone pilot.Monville said one of the biggest challenges will be recovering the main wreckage from the impact crater in the roadway. Water in the crater following heavy rainfall is complicating access to the wreckage.Investigators expect their work at the scene to continue for several days.The NTSB is asking anyone who witnessed the crash or has relevant photographs or video to contact investigators at witness@ntsb.gov. Anyone who finds aircraft debris is being asked not to move it and instead contact authorities.Chapman emphasized that investigators will not determine the probable cause while working at the scene."Our mission is to understand not just what happened, but why it happened and to recommend changes to prevent it from happening again," Chapman said.

entry.title: Indian River, St. Lucie counties declare local states of emergency amid widespread flooding
entry.summary: Indian River and St. Lucie counties declared local states of emergency Monday as heavy rainfall and flooding continued to inundate roads and neighborhoods across the Treasure Coast. In Indian River County, County Administrator John A. Titkanich Jr. issued the emergency order in response to ongoing flooding, deteriorating weather conditions and continued rainfall. The county said numerous roads have become impassable, creating public safety concerns. The Indian River County emergency order took effect at 2:30 p.m. Monday and will remain in effect until further order. County officials said the declaration gives the county authority to take emergency actions, coordinate response efforts and address hazardous conditions as they develop. In St. Lucie County, officials also declared a local state of emergency Monday afternoon to expedite access to any additional resources that may be needed as flooding affects streets and neighborhoods. St. Lucie County's Emergency Operations Center is operating under a Level 2 partial activation. Public Safety personnel are coordinating with law enforcement, water management agencies and local governments in response to the flooding. Officials are asking residents to refrain from traveling Monday evening if possible and warning motorists not to attempt to drive through flooded roads. Crews are working to address problems across St. Lucie County as several streets and neighborhoods experience flooding. Indian River County issued a similar warning, urging residents to avoid unnecessary travel through flood-affected areas, obey road closures and barricades and never attempt to drive through flooded roadways. Health officials warn about floodwater The Florida Department of Health in St. Lucie County is also warning residents about potential health hazards associated with floodwaters. Health officials advise residents to avoid eating or drinking anything contaminated with floodwater and to avoid contact with floodwater, particularly if they have open cuts or sores. People who have wounds exposed to floodwater should thoroughly wash the affected area with soap and seek medical care if redness, swelling or drainage develops. Residents with flooded private wells are being advised that heavy rainfall could make their water unsafe to drink. Those who aren't sure whether flooding has affected their well should use bottled or boiled water for drinking, making ice, brushing their teeth and cleaning cuts or injuries. Public Safety personnel are coordinating with law enforcement, water management agencies and local governments in response to the flooding.Officials are asking residents to refrain from traveling Monday evening if possible and warning motorists not to attempt to drive through flooded roads.Crews are working to address problems across St. Lucie County as several streets and neighborhoods experience flooding.Indian River County issued a similar warning, urging residents to avoid unnecessary travel through flood-affected areas, obey road closures and barricades and never attempt to drive through flooded roadways. The Florida Department of Health in St. Lucie County is also warning residents about potential health hazards associated with floodwaters.Health officials advise residents to avoid eating or drinking anything contaminated with floodwater and to avoid contact with floodwater, particularly if they have open cuts or sores.People who have wounds exposed to floodwater should thoroughly wash the affected area with soap and seek medical care if redness, swelling or drainage develops.Residents with flooded private wells are being advised that heavy rainfall could make their water unsafe to drink. Those who aren't sure whether flooding has affected their well should use bottled or boiled water for drinking, making ice, brushing their teeth and cleaning cuts or injuries.Health officials also said people with septic systems experiencing slow plumbing should conserve water and avoid having their septic tanks pumped while groundwater levels remain exceptionally high.Both counties are asking residents to continue monitoring official sources as conditions change.Indian River County said protecting residents, visitors and emergency responders remains a priority and encouraged the public to monitor official county communications for further updates.

entry.title: Trump touts Reflecting Pool repairs during midterm closing arguments
entry.summary: As Republicans and Democrats were making their final pitch to voters on the eve of Election Day, President Donald Trump opted to forgo the campaign trail and instead focused on his renovations at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, drawing attention to an expensive, problem-plagued repair job in a place far away from most of the people his party wants to persuade. It was an unusual closing argument for Republicans to keep control of Congress. But it conforms with the way the president has devoted considerable time, attention and money in his second term on beautifying his Washington surroundings. Trump, wearing a white USA hat, even seemed to admit that he had spent much of his time focused on improving the capital city. We have a lot of great things planned for Washington, and I could get into the nation, but for that, you dont have enough time,' Trump said. IN CASE YOU MISSED IT | Trump bets on his rallies to help Republicans defy midterm history Instead of focusing on issues voters have said they're worried about, Trump dedicated a large portion of his remarks to his D.C. makeover and the pool, announcing its official re-opening, joking that he wanted to name it after himself, and repeating his false claims that the repair work he ordered was vandalized. After he finished his remarks on Monday, Trump stood silently as triumphant music played and held up a poster with an image of the previously algae-clogged pool. It was his last public appearance before Election Day. Democrats, for their part, were spending the last 24 hours before Election Day making their case in areas where Republicans have long dominated, while trying to contain the fallout from a messy intraparty split in Michigan. Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed was brushing aside concerns that his prospects could be hurt after his former primary opponent threw her support behind his Republican opponent Mike Rogers. In addition to giving the speech on Monday afternoon, Trump was also scheduled to participate in nine telerallies for Republicans, where he uses brief remarks on a mass phone call to plead for voters' support. Vice President JD Vance, meanwhile, hit the campaign trail with more traditional stops in New York and Ohio, where Republicans were fighting for House and Senate seats.

entry.summary: Flooding from heavy rainfall has forced election officials to relocate polling places in Palm Beach and Indian River counties ahead of the Nov. 3 general election. In Palm Beach County, voters in two precincts will report to different locations on Election Day. Precinct 6401 voters who normally cast ballots at Casa Rio Clubhouse have been reassigned to: Riviera Beach Preparatory and Achievement Academy 7071 Garden Road Riviera Beach, FL 33404 Precinct 7628 voters who normally vote at Ironhorse Country Club have been reassigned to: North County Senior Center 5217 Northlake Blvd. Palm Beach Gardens, FL 33418 Election officials said affected voters will receive an email and/or text message about the change if the elections office has their contact information. Signs will also be posted at the original polling places directing voters to their new locations. Sebastian polling place relocated Flooding is also affecting an Election Day polling site in Indian River County. The Indian River County Supervisor of Elections announced that voters assigned to Precinct 7 will not vote at their normal location, Sebastian Church of God at 281 Delaware Ave. in Sebastian. Instead, those voters are being directed to: Sebastian Elks Lodge No. 2714 731 S. Fleming St. Sebastian, FL 32958 The change was made because of flooding at Sebastian Church of God, according to the elections office. Polls will be open from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Tuesday, Nov. 3. Election officials are encouraging affected voters to go directly to their newly assigned polling locations. The Indian River County Supervisor of Elections has also posted an official notice about the Sebastian change on its website.

entry.summary: Heavy rain floods Port St. Lucie, Okeechobee roads amid Treasure Coast flood watch    WPEC
entry.article_text: Floodwaters are creating dangerous driving conditions across St. Lucie and Okeechobee counties, leaving vehicles stranded, roads underwater, and officials urging residents to stay home as more heavy rain threatens the region Monday. Lucie Police Department ( PSLPD ) is urging residents to avoid unnecessary travel as emergency crews respond to widespread flooding. Police report flooding on Southwest Airoso Boulevard, Southeast Thornhill Drive, Southworth Boulevard and Jeanette Drive, Country Club Estates, Southwest Discovery Way and Community Boulevard in Tradition, and LTC Parkway. City officials have closed California and Savona boulevards and Port St. Lucie Boulevard and Aviation Avenue, while SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard south of Gatlin Boulevard, St. Lucie West Boulevard, and Becker Road and Savona Boulevard are being monitored for possible closures as conditions worsen. "Turn around, don't drown!" police reminded residents. Officials said drivers whose vehicles become stranded in floodwaters can call a towing company directly if they are not in immediate danger and do not require rescue. Water has also been reported on Tradition Parkway, Community Boulevard, Volucia Drive, and Innovation Way, which remain open but are being monitored. City crews are checking drainage systems, responding to potholes, and urging drivers not to remove barricades or travel through flooded roadways. Motorists are being urged to avoid the intersection and use alternate routes. See also: GALLERY: Flooded roads creating challenges for drivers in Palm Beach County St. Lucie County has activated its Emergency Operations Center and issued a local state of emergency as flooding continues across the county, spokesperson Eric Gill said. "We're at a Level 2 partial activation at the Emergency Operations Center and have issued a local state of emergency to give us the means to access resources if we need them," Gill told CBS12 News on Monday. Gill said road closures continue to change as conditions evolve and urged residents to stay off the roads if possible. County offices and schools closed early Monday because of the flooding. Area Regional Transit (ART) has temporarily suspended regular transportation service due to flooding and unsafe road conditions, with officials contacting affected passengers and monitoring conditions before service resumes. For more information, visit SLCART . Lucie County schools announce early dismissal, cancel aftercare Flood watch remains in effect across the Treasure Coast According to the National Weather Service in Melbourne, east-central Florida, including Indian River County, remains under a flood watch until 7 p.m. Forecasters expect an additional 1 to 3 inches of rainfall, with some locations facing a 10% chance of receiving 5 inches or more. In Indian River County, officials are warning residents to prepare for scattered to widespread showers and thunderstorms, with periods of heavy rainfall that could lead to localized flooding of roads and low-lying areas. According to county officials, the primary weather hazards include: Heavy rainfall and localized flooding. Wind gusts of 25 to 40 mph. Dangerous beach and marine conditions. Officials said the potential for heavy rainfall and flooding could continue through Tuesday. Residents are being urged to secure loose outdoor items, allow extra travel time, slow down on wet roads and keep multiple ways to receive weather alerts. With the ground already saturated from previous rainfall, additional storms could quickly lead to standing water on roadways and worsening flooding conditions. Lucie officials are encouraging residents to monitor the city's website and the Port St. Lucie Police Department's social media channels for updates on traffic conditions and potential road closures. Okeechobee County roads remain underwater Meanwhile, several major roadways in Okeechobee County remain underwater, with officials warning that flooding could continue for several days, even after the weather improves. Authorities said warning signs have been placed in affected areas, but motorists should use extreme caution. According to county officials, the following major roads are experiencing flooding: State Road 68 East: The roadway is underwater from the 3000 block to the 15000 block. State Road 70 East: Water is covering the roadway in the 11000 block near Posey's Corner. Highway 441 North: The roadway is underwater near Potter Road. Officials stressed that these are only some of the major roads affected by flooding. Numerous local and residential streets throughout Okeechobee County also remain flooded, with some completely submerged and potentially impassable. Motorists are being warned not to assume roads outside the listed areas are safe. Floodwaters could damage roadways County officials also warned that many roads have been saturated or submerged for more than 24 hours, raising concerns about damage to pavement and underlying road structures. Prolonged exposure to floodwaters can weaken road surfaces, while standing water can conceal washouts, pavement deterioration and other hazards. Authorities said a road that was passable earlier may no longer be safe to travel. Drivers who must travel are being urged to significantly reduce their speed and avoid flooded roadways whenever possible. Officials warned that driving too fast through standing water increases the risk of hydroplaning and losing control of a vehicle. Vehicles traveling through flooded streets can also create waves that push additional water into nearby homes and properties, worsening flooding for residents. Okeechobee County residents in need of more information can contact the county call center at 863-824-6888 or the nonemergency line at 863-763-3117.

There were nine people aboard, including two flight crew members and seven passengers.The NTSB said at approximately 12:47 p.m., the crew told air traffic controllers they were encountering light clear icing that they considered manageable, along with moderate turbulence.The aircraft was flying at 35,000 feet when the crew reported altitude deviations of approximately 700 feet. They also reported an outside temperature of minus 53 degrees Fahrenheit.Shortly afterward, the crew reported encountering precipitation and asked to climb to 37,000 feet. Air traffic control approved the request."Less than 30 seconds later, a transmission from the airplane announced the descent, followed by a mayday call," Chapman said.WATCH BELOW: Gov. DeSantis speaks about tragedyAt about 12:48 p.m., investigators said the crew reported the aircraft was in an overspeed condition and descending. Later communications indicated it was rapidly losing altitude.The plane crashed at approximately 12:51 p.m. near Greenacres and Palm Springs.All nine people aboard were killed.Chapman said investigators are examining whether the icing and turbulence played a role in the crash."The weather conditions are a major focus of the investigation," Chapman said, adding that investigators still need to determine what conditions were like at the plane's cruising altitude.The NTSB has not yet confirmed whether the aircraft flew through an active thunderstorm.Chapman said investigators have "some indication that the aircraft was breaking before impact," but cautioned that the investigation remains in its early stages.The debris field was described as roughly a half-mile by four-tenths of a mile, with debris found around ball fields, businesses and residences.Investigators have not yet identified all of the aircraft pieces recovered from the scene.NTSB Investigator-in-Charge Timothy Monville said one person on the ground suffered a leg injury. The person had been inside a vehicle leaving the area immediately adjacent to the crash site, according to information provided to investigators.Investigators are also trying to determine whether a cockpit voice recorder was aboard the aircraft when it crashed.Chapman said maintenance records indicate one had been installed, but investigators still need to confirm it remained aboard the plane.If recovered, Chapman said information from the recorder could become an important part of the investigation.About 20 NTSB investigators began arriving in Palm Beach County Sunday evening, with additional personnel arriving Monday.The investigative team includes specialists in aircraft systems and structures, recorders, weather and air traffic control, as well as a drone pilot.Monville said one of the biggest challenges will be recovering the main wreckage from the impact crater in the roadway. Water in the crater following heavy rainfall is complicating access to the wreckage.Investigators expect their work at the scene to continue for several days.The NTSB is asking anyone who witnessed the crash or has relevant photographs or video to contact investigators at witness@ntsb.gov. Anyone who finds aircraft debris is being asked not to move it and instead contact authorities.Chapman emphasized that investigators will not determine the probable cause while working at the scene."Our mission is to understand not just what happened, but why it happened and to recommend changes to prevent it from happening again," Chapman said.

entry.title: Okeechobee County sees 1-in-200-year rainfall event, leaving neighborhoods underwater
entry.summary: Neighborhoods were underwater, and schools were closed Monday following heavy rains across Okeechobee County. Justin Hazellief, public safety director and fire chief for the county, said the area experienced a 1-in-200-year rainfall event, receiving around 9 to 10 inches of rain in just six hours on Sunday. WATCH REPORT BELOW: Significant flooding impacting roads, neighborhoods in Okeechobee 'This is by far in my 25 years this is the worst that I've seen,' Hazellief said. 'Mother nature has a mind of her own, and whenever she brings that amount of rain in that short of time, there's no infrastructure anywhere that would be able to handle that amount of water and not have some consequences.'  The most heavily impacted area, Hazellief said, was the southwest portion of the county.  Hazellief said the pumps are on and the locks are open at Taylor Creek to bring water levels down.  With more rain in the forecast, Hazellief said crews are working non-stop.  'They will continue to work 24/7 until we're able to restore some normalcy as far as water levels go,' Hazellief said.  Okeechobee County Sheriff Noel Stephen said they've been deploying their high-water rescue vehicles during the flood event.  'We're just trying to ask people to slow down, take a breath, and be patient,' Stephen said.  Chief Donald Hagan, with Okeechobee Police, asking people to stay out of flooded areas.  'If you don't live in that neighborhood, stay out of the neighborhood because you're pushing a wake that could inundate somebody's home,' Hagan said.  WPTV went to the Seminole Cove community, where parts of the neighborhood were completely underwater.  Neighbor Debra Mauldin said she's never experienced flooding like this before.  'It just kept pouring,' Mauldin said. 'I'm worried. I couldn't go to work this morning, but there's nothing we can do about it.'  With more potential rain in the forecast, Mauldin said she's keeping her eyes to the sky.  'Just hanging out, watching the rain, and hoping it doesn't get worse,' Mauldin said.  The Okeechobee School District said it is planning for schools to open on Tuesday.

entry.title: Indian River, St. Lucie counties declare local states of emergency amid widespread flooding
entry.summary: Indian River and St. Lucie counties declared local states of emergency Monday as heavy rainfall and flooding continued to inundate roads and neighborhoods across the Treasure Coast. In Indian River County, County Administrator John A. Titkanich Jr. issued the emergency order in response to ongoing flooding, deteriorating weather conditions and continued rainfall. The county said numerous roads have become impassable, creating public safety concerns. The Indian River County emergency order took effect at 2:30 p.m. Monday and will remain in effect until further order. County officials said the declaration gives the county authority to take emergency actions, coordinate response efforts and address hazardous conditions as they develop. St. Lucie County's Emergency Operations Center is operating under a Level 2 partial activation. Public Safety personnel are coordinating with law enforcement, water management agencies and local governments in response to the flooding. Officials are asking residents to refrain from traveling Monday evening if possible and warning motorists not to attempt to drive through flooded roads. Crews are working to address problems across St. Lucie County as several streets and neighborhoods experience flooding. entry.title: Gov. DeSantis declares state of emergency for 7 Florida counties, including Treasure Coast, for flooding
entry.summary: Gov. Ron DeSantis declared a state of emergency Monday for Indian River, Martin and St. Lucie counties as heavy rainfall and flooding continued to affect parts of the Treasure Coast. The three Treasure Coast counties are among seven covered by Executive Order 26-227. The declaration also includes Brevard, DeSoto, Hardee and Highlands counties. The governor's office said flooding has affected and could continue to affect critical infrastructure, including state and county roads, major interstates, airports and schools. Additional heavy rain and thunderstorms were also forecast, potentially worsening flooding in already affected areas. READ THE FULL EXECUTIVE ORDER BELOW: The declaration gives state and local officials additional authority and resources to respond to the flooding. It authorizes the state coordinating officer to carry out response, recovery and mitigation efforts, including logistical, rescue and evacuation operations. The order also allows the Florida National Guard and Florida State Guard to be activated as needed. The order gives the Florida Department of Transportation authority to close roads or manage traffic when necessary and allows tolls to be waived if needed to facilitate emergency assistance or evacuations. Local governments may also waive certain procedures involving public works, contracts, equipment, workers and spending to speed up their emergency response. WATCH BELOW: Heavy rain floods Port St. Lucie roads Heavy rain floods Port St. Lucie roads, leaving drivers stranded Residents in Indian River, Martin and St. Lucie counties are also covered by provisions allowing pharmacists to provide up to a 30-day emergency refill of maintenance medications. State and local facilities may be closed as necessary, and public facilities suitable for shelters must be made available if requested by local emergency management officials. The declaration also activates Florida's price-gouging protections in the affected counties for essential commodities, supplies, services and equipment needed because of the emergency. With Florida's general election scheduled for Tuesday, the order includes a provision addressing potential impacts from the flooding. Any county supervisor of elections who cannot fully comply with certain polling-place requirements must notify the Florida Department of State about proposed partial or substitute measures, which would require approval from the Florida secretary of state. entry.title: Martin County and Okeechobee County schools closed Tuesday due to flooding
entry.summary: Both Okeechobee County and Martin County Public Schools will be closed Tuesday, Nov. 3, as flooding and severe weather continue to create unsafe travel conditions across the region. MARTIN COUNTY SCHOOLS CLOSED All Martin County School District-operated schools will be closed Tuesday, which will also include all after-school activities. School officials said in a Facebook post that conditions vary significantly across the region, with some communities experiencing serious flooding and difficult travel conditions. The district said many of its employees and families live outside Martin County and commute into the county each day. Those conditions in neighboring communities played an important role in the decision to close schools. Throughout Monday, the district received reports of employees and families driving through floodwaters to get home, abandoning vehicles because of impassable roads and making alternate overnight accommodations because they could not safely remain in their homes. Officials said they also considered whether employees would be able to safely travel to and from campuses and whether schools would have enough staff and resources to safely support students throughout the day. The district said the decision follows Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis' declaration of a state of emergency covering Martin County and surrounding counties. 'We encourage everyone to use caution and prioritize their safety as conditions continue to affect our region,' the district said. Families are being asked to monitor the Martin County School District's website and social media accounts for additional updates. In a Facebook post, the district said crews spent Monday assessing school campuses and their accessibility following widespread flooding across the county. entry.summary: Flooding prompts St. Lucie County closures, could affect Election Day voting    WPEC
entry.article_text: Lucie County officials are urging residents to stay off the roads unless travel is necessary, as significant rainfall and flooding affect the area. Ron DeSantis issued Executive Order 26-227, declaring a state of emergency for St. Lucie County and six other Florida counties because of widespread flooding and threats to public safety and critical infrastructure. Lucie County Sheriff’s Office said numerous roads are flooded or impassable, with more rain expected through Monday night and Tuesday. Deputies and other personnel remain on duty and are coordinating with the Emergency Operations Center, the agency said. See also: NTSB: Learjet crew reported ice, turbulence before deadly Florida crash The sheriff’s office urged residents to stay home, never drive through floodwaters, and avoid moving or driving around barricades and road-closure signs. Residents should also stay away from downed power lines and standing water near electrical equipment, and monitor official sources for weather alerts and road updates. Lucie County Public Schools , county government offices and courthouses will be closed Tuesday, Nov. Lucie County Supervisor of Elections announced temporary polling-place changes for the Nov. 3 General Election because flooding has affected road access to some locations. Voters in the following precincts should go to their temporary voting locations: Precinct 12 , originally at Fort Pierce Masonic Lodge: Days Inn Midtown, 3224 S. Precincts 49 and 71 , originally at Oak Hammock K-8 School, and Precinct 51, originally at Disabled American Veterans Hall: Port St. Lucie Community Center, 2195 SE Airoso Blvd., Port St. Access is from Airoso Boulevard. Precincts 67 and 86 , originally at St. Lucie West Centennial High School: Indian River State College Veterans Center of Excellence, 500 NW California Blvd., Port St. Access is from Peacock Boulevard. Precinct 83 , originally at Paula A. Lewis Library, and Precinct 92, originally at The Brennity at Tradition: Tradition Town Hall, 10799 SW Civic Lane, Port St. For more information about voting or vote-by-mail ballots, visit stlucievotes.gov or call the Supervisor of Elections Office at 772-462-1500 . The agency thanked deputies, dispatchers, emergency personnel, and community partners responding to the conditions and urged residents to look out for their neighbors.

entry.summary: Hundreds of people forced from their homes after a deadly Learjet crash near Greenacres are now facing a difficult reality: they don't know when they'll be allowed back. An estimated 400 to 600 people were displaced as investigators secured the surrounding mobile home neighborhood and began combing through debris scattered throughout their houses. He says his mobile home is just about 250 feet from where the crash happened. But right now, he can't get to his house, his vehicle or the tools he needs to work. 'I have a regular life like everybody does, and all of us just want a little bit of our lives back, I guess,' Perez said.
